why_ai: Lots, garages and valet are run on site by attendants and managers, but gateless camera entry and app payment are removing booth and cashier work by 2031.
why_clarity: Occupancy, revenue per space and owner statements are measured to the cent, and the same sessions, rate changes and month-end closes repeat daily.
why_digital: The product is a physical space and on-site service bought through local owner RFPs, with payment and reporting increasingly digital.

why_ai: Running an owner's garage mixes on-site staffing with an owner relationship and rate judgement, while reporting and pricing move to software.
why_clarity: Net parking income per space is an agreed, monthly number, though how much the operator's decisions moved it is hard to separate.
why_digital: Garages are operated in person and won through local RFPs; budgets, statements and rates are handled on screen.

why_ai: Valet is people driving guests' cars at the client's door, which no camera or app replaces by 2031.
why_clarity: Parking and returning cars repeats hundreds of times a night with clear claims and complaint measures.
why_digital: A physical service delivered at a hotel or hospital entrance, bought locally by the property.

why_ai: Matching sessions, payouts and deposits and applying contract rules is screen work that reconciliation software and AI absorb readily.
why_clarity: Every dollar either reconciles or does not, every month, under written contract terms.
why_digital: Transaction files in, owner statements out, all on screen; buyers are operators and owners in the US market.

why_ai: Billing monthly parkers and reconciling validations is routine administration that billing software can automate end to end.
why_clarity: Accounts are billed or not, credentials active or not, and the same cycle repeats every month.
why_digital: Billing and credentials are digital, but access cards and hang tags are still issued physically at the facility.

why_ai: Assignments, guest passes and billing are software work, with patrols and tows the remaining hands-on part.
why_clarity: Spaces are assigned and billed per unit under clear rules, though disputes over tows are judged case by case.
why_digital: Assignments and billing run in apps and property platforms; enforcement happens physically on site.

why_ai: Small operators run lots by hand on local relationships with landowners that national and camera-based challengers find hard to displace.
why_clarity: Revenue and renewals are measurable, but each small operator runs its lots its own way.
why_digital: Physical lots run in person and won through local relationships, with cash and pay stations common.

why_ai: Hourly demand forecasting and rate rules are exactly what pricing software and AI do well, as city meter programmes already show.
why_clarity: RevPAS and occupancy give quick, objective feedback on thousands of repeated hourly decisions, though price response must be estimated.
why_digital: Gate counts and bookings in, rates published to PARCS and marketplaces, mostly on screen; street boards are still physical.

why_ai: Matching sessions and issuing recoveries is automated, but state notice laws and DPPA exposure keep accountable humans on the rules.
why_clarity: Each unpaid session is recovered, voided or lost, under written state rules, at high volume.
why_digital: Camera and payment data in, prompts and notices out, mostly digital, sold to local operators and owners.

why_ai: Charging cars automatically at exit is the automation itself; little human judgement remains once cameras and accounts work.
why_clarity: A session is paid at exit or not, instantly, thousands of times a day.
why_digital: Cameras capture physical cars, but matching, charging and member apps are fully digital.

why_ai: Notice generation is automated, but whether a notice is lawful in each state and how disputes are answered carries legal accountability.
why_clarity: Notices are collected, voided or disputed with clear outcomes, though state rules keep changing.
why_digital: Session records and motor-vehicle data in, mailed notices and dispute letters out, bought by operators region by region.

why_ai: Price and availability feeds are built by crawlers and models, protected mainly by years of surveyed records.
why_clarity: Coverage and accuracy of price and availability records are measurable and checked continuously.
why_digital: Surveys and feeds in, licensed data and APIs out, sold worldwide to car makers and map platforms.

why_ai: Recognition models are ML product work, with hardware installation and messy real-world capture as the hands-on part.
why_clarity: Read accuracy and paid-session rates are measured objectively, though edge cases vary by site.
why_digital: Images in, recognition software and gate hardware out, sold to operators nationally.

why_ai: Curb analytics and camera enforcement are software work, constrained by city policy and public scrutiny.
why_clarity: Occupancy and citations are measurable, but what a good curb policy is remains a city judgement.
why_digital: Camera and fleet data in, analytics and citations out, bought through city procurement.

why_ai: Central pricing and reporting are analyst work that revenue-management software increasingly automates.
why_clarity: RevPAS and statement accuracy are clear, recurring measures across thousands of facilities.
why_digital: Transaction data analysed on screen for internal and owner reporting.

why_ai: Marketplace pricing and demand forecasting are data-science work AI tools compress.
why_clarity: Booking conversion and fill rates give fast, objective feedback on repeated pricing decisions.
why_digital: Search and booking data in, prices and dashboards out, entirely online.

why_ai: Siting analysis mixes utilisation models with site visits; demand for charging grows with EV adoption.
why_clarity: Utilisation is measurable, but a site's payback shows only over years.
why_digital: Session and site data analysed on screen; the chargers themselves are physical.

why_ai: Counts, site walks and engineer-stamped garage designs and restoration keep accountable professionals on site.
why_clarity: Demand and rate studies follow known methods, but each site and client differs.
why_digital: Site counts and client data in, written studies and designs out, sold to local clients.

why_ai: Auditors carry professional accountability for findings, though transaction testing is increasingly automated.
why_clarity: Audit programmes are codified and findings are checked against contract terms.
why_digital: Records reviewed on screen, with some site visits, for owners in each jurisdiction.

why_ai: Acquisition and valuation judgements are high-stakes and relationship-led, with licensed appraisers signing values.
why_clarity: Deals are few and outcomes show only years later.
why_digital: Financial models and appraisals produced on screen, with property tours.

why_ai: Notice preparation and collections are high-volume routine work that automation is already replacing.
why_clarity: Each notice is paid, voided or disputed under written rules.
why_digital: Session and motor-vehicle data in, mailed notices out, bought by operators nationally.

why_ai: Parking software faces AI-built competitors; hardware installs and integrations are the stickier part.
why_clarity: Software product work with moderately defined features and release-cycle feedback.
why_digital: Software and gate hardware built and sold to operators and institutions nationally.

why_ai: Associations sell conferences, certification and community that members value for their people, not their data.
why_clarity: Certification and events are defined, but research output is occasional and loosely measured.
why_digital: Conferences and certification are largely in person; publications are digital.

why_ai: Public authority over rates, licences and enforcement stays with accountable officials, and officers work the street.
why_clarity: Rate rules and enforcement procedures are codified, with occupancy feedback each quarter.
why_digital: Meter data analysed on screen and enforcement on the street; no market purchase involved.

why_ai: Accountable underwriters price the risk, though rating tools encroach on the analysis.
why_clarity: Actuarial methods are codified, but losses develop over years.
why_digital: Claims data priced on screen, with some loss-control site visits.
